title: Australia shocked by Zimbabwe to cast T20 World Cup progress into doubt
content:
Zimbabwe conjured the first significant upset of cricket’s T20 World Cup by beating the 2021 winners Australia by 23 runs in Colombo.

Having set an awkward 170 to win, Zimbabwe reduced their opponents to 29-4 in the Group B fixture before Australia mustered a recovery of sorts courtesy of a partnership between Matthew Renshaw and Glenn Maxwell. Yet that fifth-wicket stand was curtailed on 77 and, when Renshaw departed for 65 with eight balls remaining, the game was effectively up.

Blessing Muzarabani ended with 4-17 from his four overs — he has taken seven wickets across Zimbabwe’s two games to date — with his fellow seamer Brad Evans claiming 3-23 and the run out of Matthew Kuhnemann to confirm victory with three balls remaining.

The result leaves Zimbabwe unbeaten and second in the section, with Australia third and facing a daunting game against the leaders and tournament co-hosts Sri Lanka in Pallekele on Monday. Only the top two teams qualify for the Super Eights stage of the tournament.

Opener Brian Bennett provided the foundations for Zimbabwe’s total of 169-2 with an unbeaten 64 off 56 deliveries, but it was Muzarabani and Evans who wrested the advantage early on in Australia’s reply. They removed Josh Inglis, stand-in captain Travis Head, Cameron Green and Tim David, who was returning from a hamstring injury.

Renshaw and Maxwell (31) offered Australia brief hope but, with Tony Munyonga taking a stunning full-length diving catch on the boundary to see off Ben Dwarshuis, 34 off the final two overs was beyond them and they ended up falling well short.

“Even though we only took two wickets, I thought they were a bit under par,” said Head at the post-match presentation. “Then we lost early wickets and came under pressure. They played well. I still felt like we could have reached their score and we were happy to chase that, but we put ourselves under pressure by losing wickets. There was a partnership in the middle but we left ourselves with too many.

“We’ve been here before. We saw it in 2023 (in the 50-over ODI World Cup, which Australia ended up winning) with a few defeats and injuries. We have a few guys here who were there in India in 2023. We’ll look to navigate this situation and use that blueprint again.”

Zimbabwe, who failed to reach the 2024 event after losing to Uganda at the qualification stage, have now won both of their T20 World Cup meetings with Australia, the previous victory having come in the format’s first tournament back in 2007.

“I’m very happy and very proud,” captain Sikandar Raza told journalists. “I have the feeling of a brother whose younger brothers have achieved something together. The culture, environment, and unity we’ve created in this team is amazing and to win is unbelievable.

“The boys deserve to enjoy the win today. If we stick to the same processes, and take it one game at a time, we are in a great position. But it doesn’t mean anything. The next game is now the most important one.

Zimbabwe’s final two Group B fixtures are against Ireland and Sri Lanka.
